assessment: The stipulated observations locate rework mainly in larger covers and identify a possible customer-table geometry mismatch. They do not establish causes or show that removing rework alone achieves the 32-minute median. Preserve ordered sizes, designs, purchased stock, wash durability and removable installation.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: sewing and checking an initial cover of each size before releasing the remaining cuts could prevent repeated fit errors caused by the common allowance.
openings.delta: Replace whole-batch cutting with a small calibration stage; change a size allowance only when measurements support it.
openings.prediction: If allowance mismatch contributes, initial medium or large covers will show repeatable dimensional shortfall at the reference table, and subsequent corrected covers will require fewer seam reopenings. Irregular errors would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Record intended dimensions, actual cut dimensions, sewn dimensions and separate cutting/sewing/fitting times on the initial three covers. Measure retained offcuts in both directions before and after the stipulated wash sequence. Check any allowance revision against a full-batch cutting layout measured by area before further cutting; include calibration work in batch time accounting and verify wash performance.
assumptions: Any revision retains the ordered visible design and table size.
A feasible layout stays within 8% area waste; changes remain within 350 currency units and three weeks.
Initial covers remain usable batch items.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry explain customer placement failures after actual tabletop dimensions are accounted for?
openings.delta: Distinguish a corner-pocket compatibility problem from inaccurate nominal dimensions using a separate observable fit comparison.
openings.prediction: A geometry explanation predicts failures concentrated at rounded corners despite agreement in actual length and width; a dimension explanation predicts mismatch across corner types when actual and nominal dimensions differ.
openings.probe: Request actual length, width, thickness and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing the four nominal-only orders if reachable. Compare these with orders and reference tables. Before releasing affected cuts, observe first placement of an initial cover on a measured customer table; record whether interference occurs at corners or across straight spans. Any proposed pocket revision must separately pass wash, removal, time and area-yield checks.
assumptions: The willing customers include relevant table geometries and can provide reliable measurements.
Actual measurements clarify the specified table without substituting an ordered size or design.
Customer access and any adjustment fit the existing deadline and budget.
